summary: Dominion Forestry lookout of 1921 on Joss Mountain; sources differ on abandonment in 1930 or 1931, and a 2005 restoration left it in excellent condition.

facts.design: Square lookout building on a stone foundation

access.note: Reached by a hiking trail. Shuswap Trails says recreational access is monitored and seasonal closures apply. No source says whether the building is locked.

visit.trail_note: Joss Mountain Pass trail, 7.5 km one-way from the East Trailhead. Steep forestry roads, 4WD recommended. Serious alpine backcountry hike in grizzly country.

events.note: Built by the Dominion Forestry Service, per Firelookout.ca.
Packhorse trail built to service the lookout.
Shuswap Passion gives 1930. Firelookout.ca says the lookout was abandoned after 1931. See resolved_conflicts.
Columbia Helicopters restored the lookout with a new roof and windows, in conjunction with the BC Wildfire Management Branch.

corrections.current: Built by the Dominion Forestry Branch.
corrections.proposed: Built by the Dominion Forestry Service.
corrections.why: The cited Firelookout.ca page names the Dominion Forestry Service as the builder, not the Branch.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.ca says the lookout was abandoned after 1931. Shuswap Passion says it was abandoned in 1930. The story reports both.

Firelookout.ca gives about 9 km from Joss Pass to the lookout. Shuswap Trails gives 7.5 km one-way from the East Trailhead. The sources start from different points, so the story gives both figures without comparing them.

sources.title: Hiking with the deities at Joss Mountain

notes_for_editor: Brief kind 'ground' is not changed: sources describe a summit building on a stone foundation. Shuswap Trails files the hike under Sicamous and East Shuswap, while the brief's local_unit (Regional District of North Okanagan) is kept as given; no fetched source names the regional district. The 1930 vs 1931 abandonment date is a real disagreement between Firelookout.ca and Shuswap Passion. Shuswap Trails calls the summit building 'rebuilt' and Shuswap Passion says 'restored' in 2005; the story keeps both words. No staffing or fire record was found. The BC Forest Fire Lookouts Facebook group post (June 2026) returned a login wall and was not used. The Trail Guy page returned HTTP 520.
